meta.location: The temple in the land Bountiful
principles: A departure delayed by their faces
A prayer the record refuses to reproduce

world_behind.title: The limit named is the crowd's stamina
world_behind.text: Verse 2 stops the teaching because they are weak and cannot understand all he was commanded to speak. 3 Nephi 11 opened this gathering and 3 Nephi 18:39 ends it, so the pause falls in the last third of a single unbroken day.

world_behind.title: The crowd is counted here and nowhere else in the visit
world_behind.text: Verse 25 gives about two thousand and five hundred souls, made up of men, women, and children. No other chapter of 3 Nephi 11 through 18 numbers them, and every scene from 3 Nephi 11:15 onward has to be pictured at that scale.

world_behind.title: Three peoples are on the itinerary
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 15:20 says the Father separated the other tribes from those at Jerusalem, and 3 Nephi 16:1 to 3 adds a third people he is commanded to visit. Verse 4 puts the lost tribes on the same itinerary.

world_behind.title: The healings are given once in full and once as a tally
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 26:15 reports the sick, the lame, the blind and the deaf as part of what he did before his second ascension, in a single clause. This chapter spends verses 7 through 10 on the same categories.

world_behind.title: The record marks its own limit twice, and again in chapter 19
world_behind.text: Verses 15 and 17 say the prayer cannot be written and cannot be spoken; 3 Nephi 19:32 to 34 says the same of a later one. An unwritable prayer is a recurring feature of this visit rather than one lapse in the reporting.

world_behind.title: The children are picked up again in chapter 26
world_behind.text: Verses 11 to 24 have them brought, blessed, and encircled about with fire and angels. 3 Nephi 26:14 to 16 has the same children uttering things that were forbidden to be written, nine chapters later.

words.text: Weigh something over, turn it in the mind. The record uses the word five times and the King James Bible twice, both in Proverbs. Verse 3 gives it as homework between two days of teaching.
Feeling with someone in their suffering. Treated at Alma 53:13. Verses 6 and 7 give it as the reason he stays and the reason he heals.
Lame, walking with difficulty. It appears once, here, in the record, and the King James Bible six times. Verse 7 places it in a list of nine conditions.
To bow before and give reverence. The record uses the word forty-five times and the King James Bible one hundred and eight. Verse 10 has both the healed and the whole doing it at his feet.
Made a low sound of grief. The word turns up once, here, here, and the King James Bible once, of Jesus at the tomb of Lazarus. Verse 14 attaches it to the wickedness of the house of Israel.
Take in or form in the mind. Four uses here against fourteen in the King James Bible. Verse 17 says the hearts of men cannot do it with what they had just heard.
Surrounded on every side. Its count is twenty times in this book, while the King James Bible none. Verse 24 uses it twice in one sentence, of the angels and of the fire.

phrases.term: Behold, my time is at hand
phrases.text: The first notice that the day is ending. Everything after this happens past the point he said he was leaving.

phrases.term: I perceive that ye are weak, that ye cannot understand all my words
phrases.text: A teacher stopping short of his material. The limit is in the hearers, and he says so to their faces.

phrases.term: Ponder upon the things which I have said, and ask of the Father
phrases.text: Three instructions for the night: go home, think it over, pray about it. Verse 3 adds a fourth, prepare for the morning.

phrases.term: They are not lost unto the Father, for he knoweth whither he hath taken them
phrases.text: "Lost" corrected inside the same sentence that used it. The tribes are missing to Israel and located to God.

phrases.term: As if they would ask him to tarry a little longer with them
phrases.text: Mormon describing a request nobody made. The tears are the whole of the asking.

phrases.term: My bowels are filled with compassion towards you
phrases.text: The Hebrew way of locating feeling in the body. Verse 7 repeats the phrase with mercy in place of compassion.

phrases.term: I see that your faith is sufficient that I should heal you
phrases.text: Faith measured and found adequate. Verse 9 has him heal every one brought forward.

phrases.term: The things which he prayed cannot be written
phrases.text: The record stating what it will not hold. Mormon leaves the center of the scene empty on purpose.

phrases.term: No tongue can speak, neither can there be written by any man
phrases.text: The witnesses' own words about the limit. They report the failure of speech in speech.

phrases.term: He wept, and the multitude bare record of it
phrases.text: Weeping treated as testimony. Verse 22 has him do it a second time after blessing the children.

phrases.term: They were in number about two thousand and five hundred souls
phrases.text: A head count at the end of the day. Mormon gives the composition as men, women, and children.

verses.label: v. 1–3
verses.title: The reason he gives for leaving
verses.text: He does not say he is needed elsewhere first. He says "I perceive that ye are weak, that ye cannot understand all my words" (v. 2), and the errand he sets them is homework: go home, ponder, ask the Father for understanding, "and prepare your minds for the morrow" (v. 3). The stated obstacle is capacity, and the remedy is a night.

spans.text: and prepare your minds for the morrow

verses.label: v. 5–6
verses.title: He changes his mind in front of them
verses.text: Verse 1 has his time at hand and verse 3 sends them home. Then he looks again and sees them "in tears, and did look steadfastly upon him as if they would ask him to tarry a little longer with them" (v. 5). Nobody speaks. What the record reports next is not a reconsideration but a reason: "my bowels are filled with compassion towards you" (v. 6).

verses.label: v. 7–8
verses.title: The invitation is a list
verses.text: The record gives eight named conditions and then a clause that makes the list open: sick, lame, blind, halt, maimed, leprous, withered, deaf, "or that are afflicted in any manner." Verse 9 reports the response with its own list, and the two do not match: sick, afflicted, lame, blind, and dumb. Dumb appears in the second list and not the first; halt, maimed, leprous, withered, and deaf appear in the first and not the second. Verse 8 also supplies a stated reason for the offer that is about a different continent, "ye desire that I should show unto you what I have done unto your brethren at Jerusalem." The condition is declared already satisfied before anyone moves.

verses.label: v. 9–10
verses.title: Everyone goes forward
verses.text: The multitude comes "with one accord" (v. 9), and verse 10 has both groups at his feet: "they who had been healed and they who were whole" (v. 10). They bathe his feet with their tears. The healing is where the chapter began and it is over in two verses.

cites.quote: they who had been healed and they who were whole

spans.text: they who had been healed and they who were whole

verses.label: v. 14–17
verses.title: What he says while kneeling
verses.text: Verse 14 has him groan within himself and name the trouble: "Father, I am troubled because of the wickedness of the people of the house of Israel" (v. 14). What follows "cannot be written" (v. 15), and the multitude's own account is a statement about limits: "no tongue can speak, neither can there be written by any man, neither can the hearts of men conceive" (v. 17). The chapter's centre is the part it declines to report.

verses.label: v. 21–22
verses.title: He weeps twice
verses.text: He takes the children "one by one" (v. 21) and blesses them, and the record puts a weeping on each side of it: "he wept, and the multitude bare record of it" (v. 21), then "when he had done this he wept again" (v. 22). The text does not say what either weeping was for.

verses.label: v. 23–25
verses.title: Behold your little ones
verses.text: The command is to look, and what they see when they look up is "angels descending out of heaven as it were in the midst of fire" (v. 24) encircling the children. Verse 25 counts the witnesses at "about two thousand and five hundred souls" (v. 25) and says each one saw for himself, which is the chapter putting a number on testimony it has just called unwritable.

chapter.title: The chapter happens after the end
chapter.text: Verse 1 announces his departure and twenty-four verses follow. The most-read material in 3 Nephi is what he did past the stopping point.

chapter.title: He names the limit of what they can take
chapter.text: Verse 2 gives weakness as the reason he holds words back. The restraint is described rather than hidden.

chapter.title: Tears change the schedule
chapter.text: Verse 5 has him look a second time and see what they will not say. The record makes his staying a response to their faces.

chapter.title: The healing is exhaustive
chapter.text: Verse 7 lists nine conditions and verse 9 says he healed every one. Nobody in the list is left out of the sentence.

chapter.title: The center of the chapter is blank
chapter.text: Verse 15 says the prayer cannot be written. The record makes its own silence the point.

chapter.title: Witnesses testify to what they cannot report
chapter.text: Verses 16 and 17 are the multitude's words about the failure of words. Their record is a record of insufficiency.

chapter.title: He weeps twice
chapter.text: Verses 21 and 22 both say it, with the blessing of the children in between. The repetition is the record's way of holding the moment open.

chapter.title: Children are the last thing he shows them
chapter.text: Verse 23 tells the crowd to look at their own little ones, and verse 24 gives them fire and angels. The day closes on the youngest people there.

applications.title: Stop before the hearer is full
applications.text: He held back words they were not ready for, and said so: "I perceive that ye are weak, that ye cannot understand all my words." Ending a conversation because of the listener's capacity rather than your own supply is a decision worth making on purpose.

applications.title: Give the homework with the pause
applications.text: The stopping comes with four instructions attached: go home, ponder, ask the Father, and prepare your minds for the morrow. If you postpone something, hand over the work that fills the gap, or the pause is only a delay.

applications.title: Look twice
applications.text: The first look ended the meeting and the second one changed it. He "cast his eyes round about again" and saw tears. Before you leave a room, look at it once more.

applications.title: Ask who is hurting before you leave
applications.text: He named nine conditions and then closed the list so nobody could fall outside it, "or that are afflicted in any manner." When you make an offer, add the clause that covers the person whose trouble you did not think of.

applications.title: Bring the children in
applications.text: The instruction is one sentence and the logistics take another: "the multitude gave way till they had all been brought unto him." An adult gathering does not include children by accident; somebody has to say so and somebody has to move.

applications.title: Let some things stay unwritten
applications.text: Mormon refused to record part of the prayer and said why: no tongue can speak it and no man can write it. Not every experience has to be converted into an account of the experience.

applications.title: Do it one by one
applications.text: He took the children "one by one, and blessed them, and prayed unto the Father for them," in a crowd of two thousand five hundred. Where the point is that a person was seen, there is no version that scales.

applications.title: Tell people to look at what is in front of them
applications.text: "Behold your little ones" is three words, and what follows is the thing this chapter is remembered for. Sometimes the most useful instruction is one that directs attention rather than supplying content.

questions.text: What am I trying to take in that I am not ready for?
What have I been told to ponder and have not?
Who has asked me for more time without saying so?
Which of my afflictions have I not brought forward?
What wickedness troubles me enough to groan over?
When did I last weep over someone else's children?
What have I seen for myself that I could bear record of?
